section_summary: This section documents the planning, monitoring, and policy formulation for the demilitarization and democratic reorganization of Japanese education under Allied occupation from late 1945 to early 1947. It contains SCAP progress reports, analyses of Japanese educational debates and political party platforms, State Department intelligence inquiries, and Soviet diplomatic requests for information. The section centers on the Japanese Educational Reform Council's landmark interim report establishing the 6-3-3-4 school ladder and decentralized education committees, culminating in the Far Eastern Commission's certified policy decision on educational revision.

subfiles.about: Proposals for modernizing Japanese culture, language, and adult education through expanded public libraries.
subfiles.summary: Watanabe proposes rationalizing Japanese history, standardizing technical terms, translating classics into spoken Japanese, and establishing a Monbusho Local Library Bureau for adult education.
subfiles.title: Proposal for Japanese Educational and Cultural Reform

subfiles.about: Transmittal of an attached communication concerning Japanese education to the State Department.
subfiles.summary: White House slip referring an attached matter to the State Department.
subfiles.title: White House Referral Slip

subfiles.about: Australian Government request to participate in formulating a Japanese re-education directive.
subfiles.summary: Wailes forwards an Australian note requesting consultation on a master plan for Japanese re-education, recommending informal discussions.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Australian Participation in Japanese Re-education Plan

subfiles.about: Status of women representatives in the advisory group of educators sent to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Reports on the advisory group to Japan, noting female and adult education representation.
subfiles.title: Letter Concerning Advisory Group of Educators to Japan

subfiles.about: Transmittal of a SCAP press release detailing four months of Japanese educational reform.
subfiles.summary: Bishop transmits General Dyke's press release on demilitarization, teacher screening, and educational democratization in Japan.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 283: Japanese Education Being Liberalized

subfiles.about: Public relations compilation covering fisheries evasion, textbook policy, educational liberalization, and Korean Coast Guard recruitment.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, United States Army Forces, Pacific, Public Relations Office
subfiles.summary: Reports blocking an illicit Japanese fishing scheme, textbook decentralization, General Dyke's four-month report on educational liberalization, and Korean Coast Guard recruitment.
subfiles.title: GHQ Press Release on Fisheries, Textbooks, Education Liberalization, and Korean Coast Guard

subfiles.about: Transmittal of a media analysis report summarizing Japanese magazine articles on educational issues.
subfiles.summary: Bishop transmits CI&E Publications Analysis No. 14 reviewing Japanese periodical commentary on educational reforms.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 317: Recent Japanese Magazine Articles on Education

subfiles.about: Analysis of post-war Japanese periodical articles debating educational reform, language modernization, and teacher welfare.
subfiles.from: Civil Information and Education Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: Analyzes Japanese press debates regarding purging militarist educators, replacing Kanji with Romaji, school administrative reforms, low teacher compensation, and student living hardships.
subfiles.title: Publications Analysis No. 14: Education
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.about: Report on the operational status, faculty, enrollment, and physical plant of Kobe College.
subfiles.summary: Reports Kobe College survived the war undamaged, maintained Christian services, and details its enrollment and international faculty.
subfiles.title: Report on Kobe College

subfiles.about: Approval process for shipping 300 books requested by Roland Elliott to students in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Informs Schuler that CAD will seek SCAP approval and shipping priorities once a book list is submitted.
subfiles.title: Letter Regarding Shipment of Books for Students in Japan

subfiles.about: Transmittal of a staff memorandum analyzing Japanese political party platforms regarding education.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson forwards Leebrick's study of political party platforms, student political activity, and teacher unionization.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 375: Attitude of Leading Japanese Political Parties Toward Education

subfiles.about: Survey of Japanese political party platforms, election pledges, and teacher and student political activities.
subfiles.summary: Leebrick examines educational platforms of major political parties, noting shared support for democratization and teacher raises alongside general campaign vagueness.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Attitude of Political Parties Toward Education

subfiles.about: Informant allegations of Communist influence in excluding the American Federation of Teachers from the Japan mission.
subfiles.summary: Hoover reports allegations that Communist sympathizers in the State Department excluded the AFT from the educational mission.
subfiles.title: Alleged Communist Influence in Selection of Educators for Japan

subfiles.about: Proposal to assign State Department liaison officers for information and cultural affairs to SCAP and AMGIK.
subfiles.summary: Recommends assigning OIC liaison officers to Tokyo and Seoul following the transfer of occupied area personnel.
subfiles.title: Appointment of Liaison Officers for Information and Cultural Affairs to SCAP and AMGIK

subfiles.about: Staffing structure and organization of the Reorientation Branch of the Civil Affairs Division.
subfiles.from: Reorientation Branch, Civil Affairs Division, War Department Special Staff
subfiles.summary: Diagram of positions, personnel, and functional units within the Civil Affairs Division's Reorientation Branch.
subfiles.title: Civil Affairs Division Reorientation Branch Organizational Chart

subfiles.about: Transmittal of a draft airgram to POLAD Tokyo requesting educational and religious intelligence.
subfiles.summary: Stelle submits a draft airgram requesting research data from CI&E in Tokyo via diplomatic channels.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Airgram to U.S. Political Adviser, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Department inquiries regarding Japanese teachers' unions, school attendance, and Shinto shrine leadership.
subfiles.summary: Requests data on teachers' union membership, university attendance, Shinto shrine leadership, and Christian conversions.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-132 to POLAD Tokyo on Japanese Education and Religion Research

subfiles.about: SWNCC approval and transmittal of SWNCC 108/1 regarding revision of the Japanese educational system.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring transmits approved SWNCC 108/1 on Japanese educational policy for submission to the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.title: SWN-4803: Policy for Revision of the Japanese Educational System

subfiles.about: Instruction to present SWNCC 108/1 on educational revision to the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: Instructs the U.S. member to present SWNCC 108/1 to the FEC to obtain a formal policy decision.
subfiles.title: Memorandum for U.S. Member, Far Eastern Commission: Revision of the Japanese Educational System
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: Request for copies of reports on Japanese education for the Missionary Research Library.
subfiles.summary: Fahs requests copies of 'Education in Japan' and the U.S. Education Mission report for library use.
subfiles.title: Letter Requesting Reports on Japanese Education

subfiles.about: Transmittal of requested reports on Japanese education to the Missionary Research Library.
subfiles.summary: Leverich sends copies of 'Education in Japan' and the U.S. Education Mission report to Fahs.
subfiles.title: Letter Transmitting Reports on Japanese Education

subfiles.about: Mission response stating staffing shortages prevent immediate compilation of requested education data.
subfiles.summary: Bishop reports that mission personnel shortages make immediate compilation of requested educational data impossible.
subfiles.title: Incoming Airgram No. 1214 Regarding Education and Religion Inquiries

subfiles.about: Designation of a white copy as permanent record copy replacing an unreturned action copy.
subfiles.from: Department of State Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: Official notice substituting a white copy as the permanent record copy for Airgram 1214.
subfiles.title: Central Records Replacement Sheet for Airgram 1214

subfiles.about: Duplicate permanent record copy of Bishop's airgram on personnel shortages and research delays.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate record copy of Bishop's airgram explaining delays in answering educational research inquiries.
subfiles.title: Duplicate Record Copy of Tokyo Airgram No. 1214

subfiles.about: Transmittal of Soviet Allied Council inquiries and Mission replies concerning educational decentralization.
subfiles.summary: Sebald transmits correspondence with Soviet General Derevyanko regarding Japanese educational reorganization and JERC recommendations.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 840: Request by Soviet Member of Allied Council Concerning Japanese Education

subfiles.about: Soviet Allied Council request for documents on Japanese educational reorganization and decentralization.
subfiles.summary: Derevyanko requests copies of government reorganization plans, SCAP directives, and decentralization materials.
subfiles.title: Letter Requesting Information Concerning Japanese Education Reorganization

subfiles.about: SCAP Diplomatic Section reply to Soviet inquiries concerning educational reorganization and decentralization.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson transmits the JERC interim report and details progress in implementing educational reforms.
subfiles.title: Letter Replying to Soviet Inquiries on Japanese Educational Reform

subfiles.about: Interim recommendations defining educational aims, the 6-3-3-4 school ladder, private schools, and administrative decentralization.
subfiles.summary: This interim report outlines fundamental principles for new educational legislation, the 6-3-3-4 school ladder, private school administration, and decentralized educational committees.
subfiles.title: Reorganization of Japanese Education System: Interim Report of Japanese Educational Reform Council

subfiles.about: Transmittal of the Far Eastern Commission's unanimously adopted policy decision on Japanese educational revision.
subfiles.summary: Johnson transmits the FEC policy decision on Japanese educational revision, requesting directive preparation for SCAP.
subfiles.title: Letter Transmitting Policy Decision on Revision of the Japanese Educational System

subfiles.about: Official certification of the Far Eastern Commission's policy decision on Japanese educational revision.
subfiles.summary: Formal certification by Secretary General Nelson T. Johnson attesting to the accuracy of the adopted policy document.
subfiles.title: Certification of Policy Decision on Revision of the Japanese Educational System
